The purpose of this notebook is to allow the NPS team to explore the results
from the sea level rise (SLR) inundation analysis. The data sets were processed
in `rapid_workflow.Rmd` following the pattern that has been established
for the previous rapid assessment parameters.

The SLR inundation analysis within this notebook concerns itself with exposure.
We are trying to determine what the projected inundation risk of water supplies
of national parks are.

We will start this notebook by pulling in different data sets. We will avoid
generating data here (except for those data manipulations that are necessary for
visualization). 

NOTE: We are using the combined buffers data set for this exploration file, but 
the actual dataset that is saved in `rapid_workflow.Rmd` only has the 4km buffer
considered and is in `data/rapid/outputs/inundation_exposure_{date}.csv`.

# Establish environment

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# Set up work space
source("setup.R")
mapviewOptions(fgb = FALSE)
```

# Load the datasets

You can see how these data sets were generated or loaded in `src/process_inundation_data.R`

## Read in buffered water supplies

```{r}
all_buffer_ws <- sf::st_read(here("data", "all", "coast_comp_data",
                                  "altered_water_supplies", "buff_ws.gpkg"))
```

## Interagency Task Force sea level rise (SLR) projections

### Read in the SLR projections from ITF

```{r}
slr_projections <- terra::rast(here("data", "all", "coast_comp_data", 
                                    "interagency_report", "generated_products",
                                    "itf_slr_projections_2050_83rd.tif"))
```

### Read in a coastal sample of the inundation projections

This is a CONUS coast subset of the ITF SLR projection data.

```{r}
coast_projections <- terra::rast(here("data", "all", "coast_comp_data",
                                      "interagency_report", "generated_products",
                                      "itf_slr_proj_coast_subset.tif"))
```

## Read in the buffered water supply data that is joined to the ITF SLR projection data

```{r}
# Buffered water supplies with ITF SLR projections
ws_inun_proj <- sf::st_read(here("data", "all", "coast_comp_data",
                                 "altered_water_supplies", "buff_ws_itf_slr_proj.gpkg"))
```

## Read in the inundation region data

```{r}
inun_region_bboxs <- sf::st_read(here("data", "all", "coast_comp_data", 
                                      "NOAA_SLRV_2022", "inundation_data", 
                                      "inun_region_bboxs.gpkg"))
```

## Read in the buffered water supply data with their inundation region information

```{r}
# Buffered water supplies with region for inundation projections
ws_inun_proj_reg <- sf::st_read(here("data", "rapid", "inputs", "coast_comp", 
                                     "buff_ws_inun_regions.gpkg"))
```

## Read in the SLR inundation exposure risk calculations

You could find how these data were generated in `src/calc_inundation_exposure.R`.
`calc_inundation_exposure()` function is called in `rapid_workflow.Rmd`.

The "official" results are in `official_slr_inun_exp`.

```{r}
slr_inun_exp_files <- list.files(here("data", "all", "coast_comp_data", "results"),
                                 pattern = "^slr_inundation_exp_.*\\.csv$",
                                 full.names = TRUE)

slr_inundation_exp <- read_csv(slr_inun_exp_files[length(slr_inun_exp_files)],
                               show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{r}
official_slr_inun_exp_files <- list.files(here("data", "rapid", "outputs"),
                                 pattern = "^inundation_exposure_.*\\.csv$",
                                 full.names = TRUE)

official_slr_inun_exp <- read_csv(official_slr_inun_exp_files[length(official_slr_inun_exp_files)],
                               show_col_types = FALSE)
```

# Explore...

Now that we have read in all of the data let's explore the analysis.

The data that we used for this analysis is in two parts. The first is the
projected increase in SLR for a region, and the second is the inundation
surfaces that are related to the projected increase in a region. We relate 
both of these data sets to our buffered water supplies.

## All the relevant data...

This map brings together all three components of the processing workflow: the
projected SLR severity across the coast (white to black), the NOAA inundation
regions each water supply was assigned to (colored by state), and the buffered
water supply locations (4 km in orange, 1 km in red). Together these layers show
which water supplies are in high-SLR areas and which inundation surface region
was used to assess their risk.

```{r}
mapview(coast_projections,
        col.regions = colorRampPalette(c("yellow", "red")),
        na.color = "transparent",
        layer.name = "ITF SLR Projection (mm, 83rd pct, 2050)") +
  mapview(inun_region_bboxs,
          zcol = "state",
          col.regions = colorRampPalette(c("steelblue", "mediumpurple", "darkgreen",
                                           "dodgerblue", "turquoise", "royalblue",
                                           "plum", "seagreen", "cornflowerblue")),
          alpha.regions = 0.3,
          layer.name = "Inundation Region") +
  mapview(all_buffer_ws %>% filter(buffer_km == 4),
          col.regions = "grey",
          alpha.regions = 0.5,
          layer.name = "4 km Buffer") +
  mapview(all_buffer_ws %>% filter(buffer_km == 1),
          col.regions = "black",
          alpha.regions = 0.5,
          layer.name = "1 km Buffer")
```

## New and old method comparison

This section compares `raw_pct_point_change` (4 km buffer only) from
`inundation_exposure_2026-02-20.csv` against the current official run
(`slr_inundation_exp`). Points on the diagonal indicate agreement; orange
points diverge by more than 0.01 percentage points; red points are the
top-20 largest absolute differences.

```{r}
old <- read_csv("data/rapid/outputs/inundation_exposure_2026-02-20.csv",
                show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(buffer_km == 4)

new <- official_slr_inun_exp

combo <- old %>%
  select(wsd_source_id, raw_pct_point_change) %>%
  rename(raw_pct_point_change_old = raw_pct_point_change) %>%
  inner_join(
    new %>%
      select(wsd_source_id, raw_pct_point_change) %>%
      rename(raw_pct_point_change_new = raw_pct_point_change),
    by = "wsd_source_id"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    dif     = raw_pct_point_change_new - raw_pct_point_change_old,
    abs_dif = abs(dif)
  )

outliers <- combo %>%
  filter(is.finite(abs_dif)) %>%
  slice_max(abs_dif, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE)

combo <- combo %>%
  mutate(point_color = case_when(
    wsd_source_id %in% outliers$wsd_source_id ~ "outlier",
    abs_dif > 0.01 ~ "off_line",
    TRUE ~ "on_line"
  ))


ggplotly(
  ggplot(data = combo, aes(x = raw_pct_point_change_old,
                           y = raw_pct_point_change_new,
                           text = paste0(
                             "wsd_source_id: ", wsd_source_id,
                             "<br>original: ", round(raw_pct_point_change_old, 2),
                             "<br>updated: ", round(raw_pct_point_change_new, 2),
                             "<br>dif: ", round(dif, 2)))) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray60") +
    geom_point(data = filter(combo, point_color == "on_line"), color = "green4", alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_point(data = filter(combo, point_color == "off_line"), color = "orange", alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_point(data = filter(combo, point_color == "outlier"), color = "red", alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_text_repel(data = filter(combo, point_color == "outlier"), aes(label = wsd_source_id), size = 3, max.overlaps = Inf) +
    labs(x = "Original Approach", y = "New Approach"),
  tooltip = "text")

```

## Distribution of inundation metrics

Overlapping histograms (orange = 1 km, dark green = 4 km) for the four core
metrics, filtered to water supplies that were part of the inundation analysis
(`!is.na(inun_change)`). The qualitative bar charts show counts of each
`inun_change` and `inun_centroid_change` category by buffer size.

```{r}
buff_1km <- slr_inundation_exp %>%
  filter(buffer_km == 1)

buff_4km <- slr_inundation_exp %>%
  filter(buffer_km == 4)

buffer_colors <- c("1" = "orange", "4" = "darkgreen")
buffer_labels <- c("1" = "1 km", "4" = "4 km")

buffer_theme <- theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 9),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

# --- Quantitative Histograms ---

make_buffer_hist <- function(col, title_label) {
  slr_inundation_exp %>%
    filter(!is.na(inun_change)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = .data[[col]], fill = factor(buffer_km))) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 30, alpha = 0.6, position = "identity", color = NA) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = buffer_colors, labels = buffer_labels, name = "Buffer") +
    labs(title = title_label, x = NULL, y = "Count") +
    buffer_theme
}

p_ref  <- make_buffer_hist("raw_coverage_pct_ref",  "Reference Coverage (%)")
p_proj <- make_buffer_hist("raw_coverage_pct_proj", "Projected Coverage (%)")
p_cell <- make_buffer_hist("raw_cell_change",       "Cell Change (proj - ref)")
p_pct  <- make_buffer_hist("raw_pct_point_change",  "Pct Point Change (proj - ref)")

(p_ref + p_proj) / (p_cell + p_pct) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# --- Qualitative Bar Charts ---

p_inun_change <- slr_inundation_exp %>%
  filter(!is.na(inun_change)) %>%
  count(inun_change, buffer_km) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = inun_change, y = n, fill = factor(buffer_km))) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = buffer_colors, labels = buffer_labels, name = "Buffer") +
  labs(title = "Inundation Change Category", x = NULL, y = "Count") +
  buffer_theme

p_centroid_change <- slr_inundation_exp %>%
  filter(!is.na(inun_centroid_change)) %>%
  count(inun_centroid_change, buffer_km) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = inun_centroid_change, y = n, fill = factor(buffer_km))) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = buffer_colors, labels = buffer_labels, name = "Buffer") +
  labs(title = "Centroid Inundation Change", x = NULL, y = "Count") +
  buffer_theme

p_inun_change + p_centroid_change +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Water supply analysis coverage map

This map checks that NAs in `raw_coverage_pct_ref` reflect water supplies
that are genuinely outside the inundation analysis (non-coastal) rather than
a bug in the calculation. Grey points were never assigned an inundation region;
green points were in the analysis but had zero inundation in the reference
scenario; red points had measurable inundation. The inundation region bounding
boxes are shown for spatial reference.

```{r}
join_buff <- all_buffer_ws %>%
  filter(buffer_km == 4) %>%
  select(wsd_source_id) %>%
  distinct(wsd_source_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

ws_centroids <- join_buff %>%
  left_join(
    official_slr_inun_exp %>%
      filter(buffer_km == 4 | is.na(buffer_km)) %>%
      select(wsd_source_id, raw_coverage_pct_ref, raw_coverage_pct_proj),
    by = "wsd_source_id"
  ) %>%
  st_centroid() %>%
  mutate(risk_category = case_when(
    is.na(raw_coverage_pct_ref) ~ "Not in analysis",
    raw_coverage_pct_ref == 0   ~ "In analysis, no risk",
    TRUE                        ~ "In analysis, at risk"
  ))
```

```{r}
mapview(inun_region_bboxs,
        col.regions  = "steelblue",
        alpha.regions = 0.2,
        layer.name   = "Inundation Regions") +
  mapview(ws_centroids %>% filter(risk_category == "Not in analysis"),
          col.regions = "grey",
          layer.name  = "Not in analysis") +
  mapview(ws_centroids %>% filter(risk_category == "In analysis, no risk"),
          col.regions = "green",
          layer.name  = "In analysis, no risk") +
  mapview(ws_centroids %>% filter(risk_category == "In analysis, at risk"),
          col.regions = "red",
          layer.name  = "In analysis, at risk")
```

## Let's make a mapping function to look at the results.

`plot_inun_exposure()` renders an interactive mapview map for a single water
supply. The red outline is the buffer polygon; light blue cells are flooded
in the reference scenario; dark blue cells are flooded in the projected
scenario. Sites with no inundation in either scenario render only the buffer
outline. The function handles sites that span multiple NOAA inundation tiles
by loading all relevant tiles, cropping and masking each to the buffer, then
mosaicking with `fun = "max"`.

```{r}
plot_inun_exposure <- function(wsd_source_id_input,
                               buffer_km_input = 4,
                               ws_reg = ws_inun_proj_reg,
                               raster_dir = here("data", "rapid", "inputs", "coast_comp", "Extent_Rasters"),
                               maxpixels = 1e7) {

  # Get all inundation region rows for this water supply — may span multiple tiles
  ws_info <- ws_reg %>%
    filter(wsd_source_id == wsd_source_id_input,
           buffer_km == buffer_km_input,
           !is.na(proj_file))

  if (nrow(ws_info) == 0) stop("No matching water supply found in ws_inun_proj_reg")

  # Buffer polygon for cropping (geometry is the same across rows, take first)
  buffer_poly <- ws_info %>% slice(1)

  # Helper: load all tiles for a scenario, crop/mask each to buffer, mosaic if needed
  load_and_crop <- function(file_col) {

    tile_paths <- file.path(raster_dir, ws_info$state, ws_info[[file_col]]) %>% unique()

    tile_list <- lapply(tile_paths, function(p) {
      if (!file.exists(p)) return(NULL)
      r        <- terra::rast(p)
      poly_prj <- sf::st_transform(buffer_poly, terra::crs(r))
      r_crop   <- tryCatch(terra::crop(r,  poly_prj),             error = function(e) NULL)
      if (is.null(r_crop) || all(is.na(terra::values(r_crop))))  return(NULL)
      r_mask   <- tryCatch(terra::mask(r_crop, terra::vect(poly_prj)), error = function(e) NULL)
      if (is.null(r_mask) || all(is.na(terra::values(r_mask))))  return(NULL)
      r_mask
    })

    tile_list <- Filter(Negate(is.null), tile_list)
    if (length(tile_list) == 0) return(NULL)
    if (length(tile_list) == 1) return(tile_list[[1]])
    terra::mosaic(terra::sprc(tile_list), fun = "max")
  }

  ref_crop  <- load_and_crop("ref_file")
  proj_crop <- load_and_crop("proj_file")

  # Buffer polygon in WGS84 for mapview overlay
  buffer_wgs84 <- sf::st_transform(buffer_poly, 4326)

  # Start with buffer outline — always shown
  m <- mapview(buffer_wgs84,
               color         = "red",
               alpha.regions = 0,
               lwd           = 2,
               layer.name    = paste0(wsd_source_id_input, " (", buffer_km_input, " km)"))

  # Only add raster layers if they contain flooded cells (all-NA rasters cause
  # mapview to error when computing breaks)
  if (!is.null(proj_crop) && any(!is.na(terra::values(proj_crop)))) {
    m <- m + mapview(proj_crop,
                     col.regions = colorRampPalette(c("darkblue", "darkblue")),
                     na.color    = "transparent",
                     maxpixels   = maxpixels,
                     legend      = FALSE,
                     layer.name  = "Projected")
  }

  if (!is.null(ref_crop) && any(!is.na(terra::values(ref_crop)))) {
    m <- m + mapview(ref_crop,
                     col.regions = colorRampPalette(c("lightblue", "lightblue")),
                     na.color    = "transparent",
                     maxpixels   = maxpixels,
                     legend      = FALSE,
                     layer.name  = "Reference")
  }

  gc()
  return(m)
}
```


## Let's get some examples to plot

The dataframes below pull out the most interesting subsets from
`slr_inundation_exp` — top movers by different metrics, and one example each
of the `inun_change` and `inun_centroid_change` edge cases. Use these data
frames to look for interesting regions to pass into the `plot_inun_exposure()`
function.

### Biggest percent point change

Water supplies with the largest percentage point increase in inundation
coverage (projected minus reference). This is the most intuitive measure of
"how much more of the buffer gets flooded."

```{r}
most_pct_point_change <- slr_inundation_exp %>%
  group_by(buffer_km) %>%
  slice_max(rank_pct_point_change, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(wsd_source_id, buffer_km, rank_pct_point_change,
         raw_coverage_pct_ref, raw_coverage_pct_proj, raw_pct_point_change)
```

```{r}
top_pct_point_change_id <- most_pct_point_change %>%
  filter(buffer_km == 4) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  pull(wsd_source_id)

plot_inun_exposure(top_pct_point_change_id)
```

### Biggest starting inundation percentage

Water supplies with the highest reference-scenario flood coverage — i.e.,
the most already-inundated sites today. High starting coverage may indicate
areas that are already substantially at risk before accounting for future SLR.

```{r}
most_ref_coverage <- slr_inundation_exp %>%
  group_by(buffer_km) %>%
  slice_max(rank_coverage_pct_ref, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(wsd_source_id, buffer_km, rank_coverage_pct_ref,
         raw_coverage_pct_ref, raw_coverage_pct_proj, raw_pct_point_change)

top_ref_coverage_id <- most_ref_coverage %>%
  filter(buffer_km == 4) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  pull(wsd_source_id)

plot_inun_exposure(top_ref_coverage_id)
```

### Biggest projected inundation percentage

Water supplies with the highest projected flood coverage under the assigned
SLR scenario. Unlike percent point change, this captures sites that were
already heavily inundated and remain so, as well as those that newly become
inundated.

```{r}
most_proj_coverage <- slr_inundation_exp %>%
  group_by(buffer_km) %>%
  slice_max(rank_coverage_pct_proj, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(wsd_source_id, buffer_km, rank_coverage_pct_proj,
         raw_coverage_pct_ref, raw_coverage_pct_proj, raw_pct_point_change)

top_proj_coverage_id <- most_proj_coverage %>%
  filter(buffer_km == 4) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  pull(wsd_source_id)

plot_inun_exposure(top_proj_coverage_id)
```

### `inun_change` category examples

Three dataframes slice `slr_inundation_exp` by categorical outcomes.
`inun_change` uses `no_to_no / no_to_some / some_to_some / some_to_no`
to describe buffer-level inundation transitions. `inun_centroid_change`
uses `no_to_no / no_to_yes / yes_to_yes / yes_to_no` for the same logic
applied to the water supply point itself.

```{r}
# Inundation change examples
inun_change_examples <- slr_inundation_exp %>%
  group_by(inun_change, buffer_km) %>%
  slice_max(rank_pct_point_change, n = 5, with_ties = F) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(inun_change), !is.na(buffer_km)) %>%
  select(wsd_source_id, buffer_km, inun_change, rank_pct_point_change,
         raw_coverage_pct_ref, raw_coverage_pct_proj, raw_pct_point_change)

# Inundation centroid change examples
inun_centroid_change_examples <- slr_inundation_exp %>%
  filter(!is.na(inun_centroid_change), buffer_km == 4) %>%
  group_by(inun_centroid_change) %>%
  slice_max(rank_pct_point_change, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(wsd_source_id, buffer_km, inun_centroid_change, rank_pct_point_change,
         raw_coverage_pct_ref, raw_coverage_pct_proj, raw_pct_point_change)

# Combined inundation change and centroid change examples
combined_inun_change_examples <- slr_inundation_exp %>%
  filter(!is.na(inun_change), !is.na(inun_centroid_change), buffer_km == 4) %>%
  group_by(inun_centroid_change, inun_change) %>%
  slice_max(rank_pct_point_change, n = 3, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(wsd_source_id, buffer_km, inun_change, inun_centroid_change, rank_pct_point_change,
         raw_coverage_pct_ref, raw_coverage_pct_proj, raw_pct_point_change)
```

```{r}
top_centroid_id <- combined_inun_change_examples %>%
  filter(
    inun_change == "some_to_some",
    inun_centroid_change == "no_to_yes",
    buffer_km == 4) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  pull(wsd_source_id)

plot_inun_exposure(top_centroid_id)
```

## Double check that data that was analysed but is no-to-no actually doesn't have missed data somehow

Sites with `inun_change == "no_to_no"` should have `raw_coverage_pct_ref` and
`raw_coverage_pct_proj` equal to 0, not NA. NA would indicate the raster
extraction failed or the buffer fell outside all inundation tiles — which would
be a data gap, not a true zero. The summary below confirms this, and the map
spot-checks a random site to visually verify the buffer genuinely has no
flooded cells in either scenario.

```{r}
no_to_no <- slr_inundation_exp %>%
  filter(inun_change == "no_to_no")

no_to_no %>%
  summarise(
    n             = n(),
    any_na_ref    = any(is.na(raw_coverage_pct_ref)),
    any_na_proj   = any(is.na(raw_coverage_pct_proj)),
    all_zero_ref  = all(raw_coverage_pct_ref == 0),
    all_zero_proj = all(raw_coverage_pct_proj == 0)
  )
```

```{r}
set.seed(42)
sample_no_to_no_id <- no_to_no %>%
  filter(buffer_km == 4) %>%
  slice_sample(n = 1) %>%
  pull(wsd_source_id)

plot_inun_exposure(sample_no_to_no_id)
```
